scope: Theorem 7.3 of the manuscript “A Fully Polynomial Randomized Approximation Scheme for Perfect Matchings in General Graphs” (preprints/A-Fully-Polynomial-Randomized-Approximation-Scheme-for-Perfect-Matchings-in-General-Graphs-September-23-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 113 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1510b15725ee7e92), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 31-32. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Define T, q, M by Equations (7.3) and (7.6), and put Λ = 10Nq(T + 1) ( K + ⌈log2(ND + 2)⌉ + 1 ) , (7.14) s(ξ) = ⌈ 20LM ( Λ + ⌈log2(1/ξ)⌉ + 1 )⌉ (0 < ξ < 1). (7.15) 31 Initialize all slots to any one colored perfect matching and run the exact chain for s(ξ) steps. The resulting product law is at total variation distance at most ξ from ν. In particular, any top-tier slot has law within ξ of the desired weighted matching law. All tables, state representations, and transition probabilities are computable by rational arith- metic. Their sizes, arithmetic operation counts, and rational bit lengths are polynomial in N, D, K, btree, log(1/ξ), and the bit lengths of the reference activities. Exact rational choices here define an ideal process; the bounded-bit implementation in Section 9 adds at most ξ to the total variation error.
